blocking_findings.title: The same Shabbat-marked segment is bound to a canonical identity in one record and left unbound in the canonical host
blocking_findings.detail: In musaf_areshet_sefatenu/en, the record whose urn is the canonical prayer urn:x-opensiddur:text:prayer:areshet_sefatenu, segment index 1 is marked and has the condition holiday-aggregate {shabbat:true}. Its text_sha256 is 19565795d1f0…, 15 characters, but the segment has no 'canonical' attribute. In musaf_repetition_zikhronot_areshet/en, a segment with the same hash, same character count, same condition and same marked status is bound canonical=urn:x-opensiddur:text:prayer:areshet_sefatenu/zikhron. Its source_fidelity attesting_controls list only musaf_repetition_shofarot_areshet and musaf_repetition_zikhronot_areshet; musaf_areshet_sefatenu is left out, in both he and en. The canonical_parts host musaf_areshet_word_parts declares only the /opening and /conclusion parts, with no /zikhron part. So inside this scope, /zikhron is used as a canonical identity, but neither the canonical host nor the canonical-parts host declares it, and the canonical prayer realization contains a conditional segment with no part identity at all.

blocking_findings.title: A conditional segment in the canonical host has no source-fidelity review
blocking_findings.detail: source_fidelity in musaf_areshet_sefatenu/en covers only segment_index 0 (/opening) and 2 (/conclusion). Segment index 1 is marked and conditioned on Shabbat, and no fidelity or attestation entry covers it, even though the matching segment in the zikhronot record is attested. That segment's binding (or deliberate non-binding) and its condition scope have had no semantic review. This record's changed_fields include 'unit' and 'source_fidelity', so this is a current change, not carried forward from an accepted payload.

blocking_findings.title: Canonical prayer-namespace conditions are named after this publication's printing layout
blocking_findings.detail: Wording-selection and variant-reading conditions sit in the canonical prayer namespace, for example urn:x-opensiddur:condition:prayer:areshet_sefatenu/conclusion/{he,en}/first_printing and …/{he,en}/zikhronot_printing. 'first_printing' and 'zikhronot_printing' describe where this mahzor happens to print each wording, not a liturgical distinction, and they mean nothing for any other publication. The conditions are also split by language (he/en are always set together in every settings and wording_selection block), while the third condition, …/conclusion/teqiot_veseder_shofarot, is not split by language. This is the kind of publication-specific canonical identity and inappropriate condition encoding this review is supposed to catch. The conditions should express the liturgical distinction (the section context or wording variant) without publication-layout or per-language terms, or be moved to a publication-scoped namespace.

nonblocking_findings.detail: These new records bind via 'source'=urn:x-opensiddur:text:prayer:amidah/avodah/retzeh with source_fidelity=[] and corrections=[]. If 'source' only asserts derivation, not identity, this is acceptable. If it implies textual identity with the shared canonical Retzeh, a fidelity or attestation entry is needed. Please confirm what 'source' means. The he/en pair is otherwise consistent: same urn, stem, title and source, and scans s308/s309 both on p144.

The variant 'printed' fields are not masked (they contain full Hebrew and English text), unlike the rest of the projection. Their lengths (he 70, en 99 characters) match the first_printing readings, not the zikhronot_printing readings (71 and 98), even though 'printings' lists p136/p144. This is consistent if 'printed' means the host lemma, but the field's meaning should be documented. The variant ids end in '_conclusion_zikhronot' yet each holds three readings, including teqiot_veseder_shofarot.
source_scans lists only same-language scans (he: s274/s292/s308; en: s275/s293/s309), but each record's variants array also cites the other language's printings.

condition_instruction 'אַם שַׁבָּת.' is tagged condition_instruction_language='de-Hebr' (German in Hebrew script). That is plausible for a Judeo-German rubric and is consistent between the segment, the enclosing_scopes and the attesting_controls. I could not confirm the tag against the scan in this scope.

For unmarked segments, literal_sha256 differs from the fragment text_sha256 (for example opening: 2fda3f… vs f7dc3b…). For marked segments, literal_sha256 equals the fragment hash and literal_content_sha256 is a separate value. The scheme is applied consistently across records, but the projection does not document which hashing domain each field uses.

scope_limitations: final_sha256 hashes the complete unmasked payload, which I did not have, so I could not verify it.
Text values appear only as SHA256 and character counts, so I checked binding consistency by matching hashes across records, not by reading words.

The records for musaf_repetition_shofarot_areshet, musaf_areshet_sefatenu/he and any declaration of …/areshet_sefatenu/zikhron outside these seven files were not assigned. B1 is judged from the assigned records only.
I did not check global order, documentary-instruction and navigation hashes beyond confirming they are identical in all seven records. Those belong to the order group.
Out of scope: no code review and no export approval.
verdict: Not approved. The global hashes, settings, wording-selection blocks, page/scan parity between he and en, and variant reading hashes are internally consistent: first_printing, zikhronot_printing and teqiot readings each match their host fragments. However, the Shabbat 'zikhron' segment is bound to a canonical identity in the zikhronot realizations, while the identical segment in the canonical host is unbound and has no fidelity review, and the canonical-parts host does not declare that identity (B1, B2). The canonical prayer-namespace conditions also encode this publication's printing layout and are split by language (B3). Those three issues need fixing or explicit justification before these bindings can be accepted.
